parts.text: Aventuras de Sherlock Holmes XX\. — El jorobado {{#verano e:watson q:verano|Una noche de verano, pocos meses después de [[boda_de_watson|mi boda]], estaba yo sentado junto a mi propio hogar fumando una última pipa y cabeceando sobre una novela, pues la jornada había sido agotadora.}} {{#arriba e:esposa q:arriba|[[esposa|Mi mujer]] ya había subido, y el ruido de la cerradura de la puerta del vestíbulo, un rato antes, me había dicho que también los criados se habían retirado.}} {{#reloj q:reloj|Miré el reloj: eran las doce menos cuarto.}} {{#umbral e:holmes q:umbral|Para mi asombro, era [[holmes|Sherlock Holmes]] quien estaba en el umbral.}} —¡Hum! {{#arcadia e:holmes q:arcadia|¡Sigue usted fumando la mezcla Arcadia de sus tiempos de soltero!}} {{#panuelo e:holmes q:panuelo|Nunca pasará usted por un civil de pura cepa mientras conserve la costumbre de llevar el pañuelo en la manga.}} Siento ver que ha tenido usted en casa al obrero británico. ¿No serán los desagües? —No, el gas. —¡Ah! {{#clavos e:holmes q:clavos|Le ha dejado en el linóleo dos marcas de los [[clavo_de_bota|clavos de la bota]], justo donde da la luz.}}

src_en.verano: One summer night, a few months after my marriage, I was seated by my own hearth smoking a last pipe and nodding over a novel, for my day’s work had been an exhausting one.
src_en.arriba: My wife had already gone upstairs, and the sound of the locking of the hall door some time before told me that the servants had also retired.
src_en.reloj: I looked at the clock. It was a quarter to twelve.
src_en.umbral: To my astonishment it was Sherlock Holmes who stood upon my step.
src_en.arcadia: You still smoke the Arcadia mixture of your bachelor days then!
src_en.panuelo: You’ll never pass as a pure-bred civilian as long as you keep that habit of carrying your handkerchief in your sleeve.
src_en.clavos: He has left two nail-marks from his boot upon your linoleum just where the light strikes it.
src_en.criatura: out there slipped a beautiful reddish-brown creature, thin and lithe, with the legs of a stoat, a long, thin nose, and a pair of the finest red eyes that ever I saw in an animal’s head.
src_en.cobras: Snake-catcher is what I call them, and Teddy is amazing quick on cobras.
src_en.apoplejia: The medical evidence showed conclusively that death was due to apoplexy.
src_en.superficial: Oh, remarkably superficial,” said Holmes, smiling.
src_en.david: There’s one thing,” said I, as we walked down to the station. “If the husband’s name was James, and the other was Henry, what was this talk about David?
src_en.reproche: It was evidently a term of reproach.
src_en.urias: You remember the small affair of Uriah and Bathsheba?
